Ten years after Britain voted to leave the European Union, London and Brussels have struck a deal to bring their economies closer.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham says Brexit “has not worked” and would like to see Britain rejoin in his lifetime.

But not in this parliament, and he is sticking to the Labour Party’s red lines on the single market, the customs union and free movement.

Critics say he has no mandate to reopen the debate. Burnham says it is up to voters.

United States President Donald Trump welcomed the Brexit vote. Now his tariffs are one reason Britain and the EU see more to gain together.

articles.title: Big Ten faces one-bid nightmare in CFP rankings as SEC eyes four bids and Big 12 could thrive
articles.excerpt:
Bruce Pearl joins Dan Dakich to talk about the wild saga between SEC and LSU, with the conference threatening to KICK LSU out for good.

The Big Ten did itself no favors last weekend, with UCLA and In...
articles.body_text:
Bruce Pearl joins Dan Dakich to talk about the wild saga between SEC and LSU, with the conference threatening to KICK LSU out for good.

The Big Ten did itself no favors last weekend, with UCLA and Indiana both losing on the road. On Tuesday night, the College Football Playoff committee delivered another reminder of how precarious the conference’s postseason position has become.

If you were wondering what chaos could look like over the final few weeks of the season, the Big Ten is living it.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Only one of its teams sits inside the top 12 of the latest CFP rankings, and there is a scenario in which the conference that produced the past three national champions sends just one team to the playoffs.

A $17 MILLION BILL FOR AN AD WHO NEVER ACTUALLY STARTED? MICHIGAN'S TREV ALBERTS MESS GETS UGLIER

All the while, it's the SEC that is thriving this week, even if that means we're still having to figure out why Alabama is ranked that far ahead of Tennessee thanks to the 'pod' system.

Though it was interesting to see Texas leap Alabama in the rankings given they have not played each other this season, so head-to-head metrics were not used.

The bigger picture involves the Big 12 and ACC, which combine to hold five spots inside this week’s top 12, led by No. 2 Utah.

SEC THREATENS THE NUCLEAR OPTION AS LSU’S REBELLION PUTS CONFERENCE FUTURE AT RISK, RJ LUIS PLANS TO SUE

Would either one of them receive more bids than the Big Ten?

The latest CFP rankings seem to indicate we are heading down that path, unless pandemonium unfolds over the next five days during "rivalry week" across the sport.

After three weeks of arguing, the CFP committee finally corrected course around the Tennessee and Alabama situation.

The Vols moved to fifth in the latest rankings, while Alabama dropped to sixth, with Texas leaping them both to third.

But, what about those Longhorns? If Texas were to play for an SEC championship next week, a loss to No. 1 Georgia would not hurt their chances of making the CFP. Now, they had better beat Texas A&M this weekend, or the Longhorns could fall straight out of the postseason.

As for Tennessee, if the Vols take care of Vanderbilt this weekend on the road in Nashville, it will be hosting a playoff game in December.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S QUIET SATURDAY TURNS INTO A BIG TEN DISASTER WITH BRUTAL CFP CONSEQUENCES

The whole 'eye test' thing was obviously starting to agitate folks, but Hunter Yurachek did note that outside noise does not factor into any decisions made by the committee, which I guess is a good thing to know given the reaction on social media recently.

"I think we all know what we signed up for in the committee room, but I'll say there is very little impact from the outside noise on what we do every Monday and Tuesday."

TENNESSEE JUMPS, ALABAMA DROPS, INDIANA AND UCLA TUMBLE IN NEW COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF TOP 25 POLL

Dejuan Lane (10) of the Tennessee Volunteers celebrates after recovering the ball against the Alabama Crimson Tide during the first half at Neyland Stadium on Oct. 17, 2026, in Knoxville, Tenn. (Camden Hall/Getty Images)

When Alabama and Auburn get together for the "Iron Bowl," just about anything can happen.

And, even with Texas A&M looking like a $40 million waste of space this season, I wouldn’t put it past them to give the Texas Longhorns a scare, for at least three quarters.

For No. 1 Georgia, head coach Kirby Smart will have his Bulldogs ready to pounce on Georgia Tech, though I have seen a few wild endings out of that one.

There is a massive conundrum facing the conference, who has won the last three national championships.

After losing to Washington this past weekend, Indiana took a massive drop to 14th in the latest rankings. That means, unless there is pure bedlam in front of the Hoosiers, or they backdoor their way into the Big Ten championship game, the defending champions will not make the playoff.

"Indiana has two top 25 wins, but the strength of their schedule impacts their profile," CFP's Hunter Yurachek said about Indiana.

That means Indiana has dropped eleven spots after a bye-week and a three-point loss to a now-ranked opponent, which I'm sure Curt Cignetti will have thoughts about this week.

It's No. 9 UCLA that is walking a very fine line heading into a showdown with No. 15 USC this weekend in Los Angeles. What do the committee think about quarterback Ty Dieffenbach potentially missing a few games due to injury?

"UCLA fell from 4 to 9 because they lost in triple-overtime to Michigan. We will take that into consideration moving forward," CFP's Hunter Yurachek said on Tuesday night.

If the Bruins lose this weekend to USC, it doesn’t look as though they would make the field once the final rankings come out, if they were to miss the Big Ten title game.

Ty Dieffenbach No. 14 of the UCLA Bruins is embraced by a teammate as he leaves the field on a stretcher during overtime against the Michigan Wolverines at Michigan Stadium on Nov. 21, 2026, in Ann Arbor, Mich. (Getty Images)

If you're looking for a team to make a run, I think Dan Lanning might have you covered.

The way this No. 12 Oregon Ducks team is playing right now, they could be the Big Ten's only legitimate team to contend for a national championship, given they win out.

Overall, the Big Ten has just a few good teams this season, and not one that stands out as dominating after nearly four months of football.

Now, we wait to see how this weekend plays out, with even Iowa having an outside shot at making the conference title game.

That's right, No. 10 BYU is still thriving off the win over No. 4 Notre Dame, and rightfully so. Even with the overtime win over Kansas, it was going to be hard for No. 11 Texas Tech to jump the Cougars.

It's still No. 2 Utah holding the conference steady, with one final regular season game this weekend before a trip to the conference title game.

Where things could get crazy is if Texas Tech were to play Utah in the Big 12 title game, and then beat the Utes. This could potentially lead to the conference receiving three spots in the CFP, which would be a dream scenario for Big 12 members.

As for the ACC, it comes down to No. 6 Miami and No. 9 Wake Forest.

These two teams will fight for a conference title next weekend, and if both of them can close out the regular season with a win, they will both get an invite to the CFP. Also, the Demon Deacons are one of the hottest teams in the country right now, so seeding will be on the minds of plenty of teams who could be hosting a playoff game.

Wake Forest Demon Deacons quarterback Gio Lopez (3) drops back to pass during a college football game between the Wake Forest Demon Deacons and the Louisville Cardinals on September 26, 2026 at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium in Louisville, Ky.  (Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

After Boise State essentially handed San Diego State a victory this past weekend thanks to some interesting play-calling in the final minutes, there are no G-6 teams currently ranked in the new Top-25 this week.

This is going to make for an interesting two weeks for a team like the Broncos.

Get ready for a monumental final weekend of the regular season in college football, as a number of conferences sweat out the next five days.

Could we reach championship weekend with only one or two Big Ten teams inside the top-12 fighting for a playoff spot?

For a conference that has spent the past three seasons celebrating national championships, that would be one heck of a reality check.

Trey Wallace is the Sr. College Sports Reporter for OutKick.

articles.title: Kilmar Ábrego García arrives in Spain, ending Trump deportation battle
articles.excerpt:
Kilmar Ábrego García, whose deportation from the US to El Salvador last year sparked a bitter deportation battle with the Trump administration, has arrived in Spain.

After the US government admitted ...
articles.body_text:
Kilmar Ábrego García, whose deportation from the US to El Salvador last year sparked a bitter deportation battle with the Trump administration, has arrived in Spain.

After the US government admitted it had wrongfully sent Ábrego García to his home country, he was returned to the US to face human trafficking charges, which were later dropped.

The administration then continued its attempts to send him to other countries, including Uganda and Ghana.

His deportation and return became a flashpoint in the debate over President Donald Trump's immigration agenda.

Ábrego García, who is married to a US citizen and lived in Maryland, came to the US illegally from El Salvador as a teenager.

Senator Chris Van Hollen, a Democrat from Maryland, visited Ábrego García while he was in the notorious Cecot prison in El Salvador in 2025 and advocated for his release.

"A year and a half ago, the Trump Administration wanted to leave Kilmar Ábrego García to rot in a Salvadoran gulag," Van Hollen said in a statement on Tuesday. "Today, Kilmar is travelling to a country of his choice, a free man - unharmed and with dignity."

In a statement, Ábrego García's lawyer said his departure was "temporary" as he had "many options to return to the United States".

"We don't expect that to happen under this administration, which we know will never give him a fair shake, but we expect that the next administration will prioritize reunifying this family and bringing him back to Maryland," the statement said.

"Where he goes from here, where he chooses to settle for the next two years while he waits out the end of this administration, will be his choice, not the administration's choice."

The BBC has contacted the US Department of Homeland Security for comment.

Ábrego García was arrested in 2019 alongside three other men and detained by federal immigration authorities. A judge granted him protection from deportation to El Salvador at the time, citing the risk of persecution by a gang there.

In March 2025, the Trump administration deported him to El Salvador, where he was held in Cecot, a prison known for its harsh conditions. The US Supreme Court then ordered the government to facilitate his return.

The administration admitted that he was deported in error and brought him back to the US where he was set to face human trafficking charges. A federal judge dismissed the case, saying Ábrego García had been charged for political reasons.

For months, he was locked in a battle over deportation with the government.

Ábrego García had repeatedly said he would be willing to be deported to Costa Rica, and the Costa Rican government had agreed to accept him as a refugee and provide him with legal status.

After reports emerged that the administration was considering sending him to Uganda, a judge barred the government from deporting Ábrego García to a third country.

At one point the Trump administration requested that the judge lift the order so that Ábrego García could be deported to Liberia, CBS reported.

articles.title: Zidane was much better than me: Bellingham after Real Madrid wonder goal
articles.excerpt:
Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham has brushed aside comparisons with football great Zinedine Zidane following his sensational goal against PSV in the Champions League.

The England international came o...
articles.body_text:
Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham has brushed aside comparisons with football great Zinedine Zidane following his sensational goal against PSV in the Champions League.

The England international came on at half-time with Los Blancos trailing and inspired a sensational second-half display, including a magnificent effort from distance, at the Santiago Bernabeu on Tuesday.

Bellingham said he “did not know” how he scored his brilliant goal, flicking the ball up on the edge of the box and slicing a stunning effort inside the far post.

Having seen an acrobatic volley blocked minutes earlier, the England midfielder controlled Kylian Mbappe’s pass with two touches in the air and curled a superb shot into ⁠⁠the far corner from well outside the area.

“I have no idea what I did,” Bellingham told RMTV. “I had the ball in a good position and thought about shooting.”

The 23-year-old, upon joining Real Madrid, took Zidane’s number five shirt in “homage” to the Frenchman, whom he admired, and some have compared his goal to a Zidane-style strike.

“I do things that you guys think are similar to Zidane, but he was much better than me,” Bellingham told reporters.

Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho hailed Bellingham’s game-changing display as the midfielder gave Mourinho credit for helping him find arguably the best form he has enjoyed at Madrid in recent weeks, with Los Blancos winning a 10th straight match, but the coach said the midfielder only had himself to thank.

“I think the main figure responsible for what Jude is today is Jude, and his teammates. I try to help a little,” said the Portuguese coach.

“He’s an absolutely extraordinary player who has everything – he has physicality, he has technique, he has tactical understanding of the game, he has ambition, he has absolutely everything and today, obviously not by himself, but he changed the direction of the match.”

“He’s an absolutely extraordinary player and for me, without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world,” Mourinho said.

Madrid’s victory over the Dutch champions maintained their 100 percent start to the league phase, in which they are provisional leaders.

Mourinho reiterated his view that it was a “scandal” that Bellingham was not ranked in the top 10 players in the world at this year’s Ballon d’Or ceremony.

Mbappe netted twice to put Real out of sight before Vinicius Jr got in on the act with a late goal, having struck the post twice earlier in the game.

articles.title: Steelers stun the NFL by announcing they are benching Aaron Rodgers and not letting him suit up for next game
articles.excerpt:
Tom Brady discusses Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers’ season so far, and asks if the 1st-place team can win the AFC North.

In what is perhaps the most shocking quarterback move of the 2026 N...
articles.body_text:
Tom Brady discusses Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers’ season so far, and asks if the 1st-place team can win the AFC North.

In what is perhaps the most shocking quarterback move of the 2026 NFL season, the Pittsburgh Steelers have benched Aaron Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph.

The club announced the move late Tuesday night, saying Rodgers will be inactive for Friday's game between the Steelers and Denver Broncos while Rudolph takes the reins of the team's offense.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

AARON RODGERS CONFIRMS HE'S RETIRING FROM NFL AFTER 2026 SEASON WITH THE PITTSBURGH STEELERS

This decision, a source said, is not injury related.

The benching was a move from coach Mike McCarthy.

McCarthy made this move one day after he told reporters, "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback."

And, look, it's not that Rodgers doesn't deserve to get evaluated like all other players. His play was obviously scrutinized and that focus includes the facts Pittsburgh has lost two consecutive games, and both Rodgers and the offense have been inconsistent for several games dating back to a Nov. 1 victory over the Cleveland Browns.

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) watches as quarterback Mason Rudolph runs a drill during practice at the team’s NFL football training camp in Latrobe, Pa., Thursday, July 24, 2025. (AP Photo/Gene J. Puskar)

But Rodgers is not exactly surrounded by great talent. His No. 1 receiver DK Metcalf this season has made more news by getting ejected from last week's game than anything he's done to help the team win.

McCarthy must explain why he believes Rudolph gives the team the best chance to win this week. His history as starter doesn't exactly suggest he's going to overcome problems Rodgers has not.

Rudolph is 9-9-1 as a starter in the NFL during his seven seasons.

Benching Aaron Rodgers sounds bizarre and the idea that's how his career might end makes it even more outrageous.

Rodgers and McCarthy have a history that dates back to their days with the Green Bay Packers two decades ago. The two won a Super Bowl together.

'WHAT THE F--K, CALL IT!': AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY CURSE AT EACH OTHER DURING HOT MIC MOMENT

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers signals a first down during the first half of an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens, Sunday, Dec. 7, 2025, in Baltimore. (AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)

When McCarthy got hired by the Steelers in the offseason, one of his first calls was to Rodgers to see if he could convince the veteran to return to the Steelers for a second season.

And Rodgers said one of the primary reasons he returned was indeed because McCarthy was hired and because of his relationship with the coach.

That was around the time Rodgers announced this would be his final NFL season. Rodgers is in his 22nd season at age 42 (he turns 43 next month).

It's not known how Rodgers reacts to this move beyond this week.

He might request his release. He might merely accept the move, although the fact the team is going to deactivate him on Friday suggests the club understands Rodgers serving as the backup and cheerleading on the sideline is not an assignment he embraces.

Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy looks on during the first quarter against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland, Ohio, on Oct. 1, 2026. (Gregory Shamus/Getty Images)

Benching a four-time MVP is not a move undertaken without considering the ramifications. Those ramifications include the fact it's hard to merely re-insert Rodgers in the lineup once he's been benched.

It causes a distraction in the locker room. It also weakens if not cripples Rodgers' standing as the unquestioned team leader.

So, what happens if Rudolph struggles? McCarthy has opened himself up to the possibility of a serious evaluation of his management if that occurs.

This marks the first time in his career that Rodgers has been benched for performance.

He spent his first three seasons backing up Brett Favre before taking over as starter in 2008 and leading Green Bay for 15 seasons (2008–2022), winning Super Bowl XLV (and Super Bowl MVP) following the 2010 season while capturing his NFL MVP awards in 2011, 2014, 2020, and 2021.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers listens to head coach Mike McCarthy during NFL practice in Pittsburgh on May 20, 2026. (Gene J. Puskar/AP)

Rodgers suffered a two-season stint with the New York Jets (2023–2024) marked by a 2023 Achilles injury before Rodgers joined the Steelers in June 2025 under then coach Mike Tomlin.

The Steelers won the AFC North title last season with Rodgers as their quarterback.

This season, Rodgers has thrown 16 TDs against six interceptions while completing 60.9 percent of his passes – that is the second-lowest completion percentage for Rodgers since he became an starter in 2008.

articles.title: Shakib, Mustafizur not among Bangladeshi players on 2027 IPL auction list
articles.excerpt: Former captain Shakib Al-Hasan and fast bowler Mustafizur Rahman are notable absentees on the list of 11 Bangladeshi cricketers who have registered for the Indian Premier League’s (IPL) upcoming playe...
articles.body_text:
Former captain Shakib Al-Hasan and fast bowler Mustafizur Rahman are notable absentees on the list of 11 Bangladeshi cricketers who have registered for the Indian Premier League’s (IPL) upcoming player auction, as tensions continue to simmer between the South Asian neighbours.

Top-order batter Towhid Hridoy leads the players, named on a list released on Wednesday, who are seeking a place in the world’s most lucrative cricket franchise league, a year after Mustafiz’s controversial removal from the IPL.

The 11 Bangladeshis feature on an initial list of 1,220 players for the December 16 mini auction in Goa, although the pool will be trimmed before franchises make their selections, the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) said.

“With 184 players already retained or picked by the franchises ahead of the auction, a maximum of 66 slots, including 25 overseas slots, are available to be filled,” the BCCI said in a statement.

Apart from Hridoy, who is enjoying great run-scoring form, Hasan Mahmud, Parvez Hossain Emon, Ripon Mondol, Rishad Hossain, Saif Hassan, Shak Mahedi Hasan, Shamim Hossain, Shoriful Islam, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, and Taskin Ahmed are on the list, according to cricket news outlet Cricinfo.

The presence of Bangladeshi names on the draft auction comes as a surprise, months after the country’s expulsion from the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup, cohosted by India.

The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) refused to send its team to India over security concerns, which followed a fallout over star pacer Mustafizur’s removal from the Kolkata Knight Riders’ roster upon the BCCI’s instructions.

Though the BCCI gave no clear reason for his expulsion, the board said it was due to “developments all around” – an apparent reference to the tensions between India and Bangladesh that soared following the ouster of former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in 2024, who then received exile in New Delhi.

The relationship between India and Bangladesh remains tense over Dhaka’s extradition request for Hasina, which New Delhi has yet to comply with.

Among the more than 1,000 players listed for auction, England all-rounder Ben Stokes is among the high-profile names, with a base price of $216,900.

Indian players dominate the initial list, accounting for 939 registrations.

Australia leads the overseas contingent with 53 players, followed by South Africa (40), West Indies (36), New Zealand (25) and Afghanistan (23).

The list also includes players from emerging cricket nations, with 13 registrations from the United States, and 10 each from the United Arab Emirates and Nepal.

Franchises will finalise their squads after the auction, which will determine the player pool for next year’s edition of the competition.

articles.title: Ford in talks with the Pentagon to supply military vehicles
articles.excerpt: Ford said on Tuesday it has held talks with the Pentagon about supplying military vehicles and other defense products to the U.S. military, as legacy automakers seek a share of fast-rising defense spe...
articles.body_text:
Ford said on Tuesday it has held talks with the Pentagon about supplying military vehicles and other defense products to the U.S. military, as legacy automakers seek a share of fast-rising defense spending amid tough competition in the auto sector.

A Ford spokesperson said the discussions were focused on supplying highly capable military vehicles and working with U.S.-based space systems contractor Revolution Space to build advanced satellites. Ford had announced on Monday a minority investment in Revolution Space.

The Wall Street Journal first reported earlier in the day that the Pentagon was in talks with General Motors, Ford and other manufacturers to help mass-produce military drones by supplying parts including actuators, engines, sensors and lidar to drone companies.

“The Department of War is actively partnering with domestic manufacturers, suppliers, and emerging tech firms to build a resilient, high-capacity industrial base that accelerates the production, deployment, and long-term sustainment of next-generation unmanned and autonomous systems,” a Pentagon official told Reuters.

Detroit’s automakers have a long history of turning mass production capabilities toward military needs, having converted factories during World War II to build tanks, jet engines and trucks.

According to the Journal’s report, GM is weighing whether to manufacture drone motors, while U.S. defense officials have met with executives at Canadian auto parts maker Magna International and other manufacturing firms, some outside the auto industry.

GM has been most interested in getting involved with military projects at the request of high-ranking defense officials, the Journal said, adding that the automaker was in talks with RTX and L3Harris on a similar deal.

GM declined to comment on the report, but said in an emailed statement that its Defense unit has extensive capabilities and scale, and that it has “demonstrated our commitment to reinforce the U.S. defense-industrial base and help address critical needs.”

Magna said it had nothing to add with regard to the report.

articles.title: Hero veteran Virginia trooper rushes to help after car plows into women in crosswalk caught on video
articles.excerpt: Courthouse surveillance video shows a red sedan hitting two women in a downtown Richmond crosswalk. State Trooper David Meehan rushes to help, keeping traffic away from the injured women. (Credit: Vir...
articles.body_text:
Courthouse surveillance video shows a red sedan hitting two women in a downtown Richmond crosswalk. State Trooper David Meehan rushes to help, keeping traffic away from the injured women. (Credit: Virginia State Police)

A forgotten stack of court papers put a Virginia state trooper in the right place at the right time when a red sedan turned into a downtown Richmond crosswalk and sent two women tumbling off its hood.

Courthouse surveillance video shared by Virginia State Police shows the two women walking through a crosswalk on Clay Street when a red sedan makes a left turn and plows into them.

Both women rolled off the hood and fell to the pavement as the car continued through the crosswalk.

ICE OFFICER HAILED AS HERO AFTER SAVING DRIVER INJURED IN MISSOURI CRASH

Courthouse surveillance video shared by Virginia State Police shows a red sedan turning toward two women moments before striking them in a Clay Street crosswalk. (X/@VSPPIO)

Trooper David Meehan, a 14-year veteran of the agency, saw the crash and rushed to keep traffic away from the injured women, state police said.

"Right place, right time!" Virginia State Police wrote on X. "We wish both a speedy recovery."

HEART-STOPPING VIDEO SHOWS OFFICERS USE UNLIKELY TOOL TO SAVE FAMILY TRAPPED IN FLOODWATERS

Meehan said in an interview shared by state police that he had left his summonses in his cruiser.

After court, he went back to get them and returned to the courthouse to drop them off.

SUSPECTED DRUNK DRIVER KILLS 2 PEDESTRIANS IN VIOLENT CHAIN-REACTION CRASH ON MANHATTAN'S UPPER WEST SIDE

Virginia State Police Trooper David Meehan recounts how he helped two women who were struck by a car outside a Richmond courthouse. (X/@VSPPIO)

"As I came out of the building, that’s when the crash occurred," Meehan said.

The women, identified in the video as a court clerk and an attorney, were seriously injured but are expected to make a full recovery, according to police.

DRAMATIC BODYCAM VIDEO CAPTURES NYPD OFFICER RESCUING WOMAN FROM TOP OF BROOKLYN BRIDGE AFTER EMOTIONAL PLEA

A street-level view of the downtown Richmond area where two women were struck by a car while crossing Clay Street. (X/@VSPPIO)

Meehan said Richmond police arrived and offered to handle the crash, but he stayed to help.

"As troopers, we are called to be selfless, engaged and aware," Meehan said. "And, so, witnessing something like that, it just made sense for me."

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

articles.title: Al Gore buys hometown Tennessee newspaper, vows to preserve local outlet's 'independent voice'
articles.excerpt:
Former Vice President Al Gore announced Monday that he is buying his hometown newspaper The Carthage Courier. (Chris McGrath/Getty Images)

Former Vice President Al Gore is buying his hometown newspap...
articles.body_text:
Former Vice President Al Gore announced Monday that he is buying his hometown newspaper The Carthage Courier. (Chris McGrath/Getty Images)

Former Vice President Al Gore is buying his hometown newspaper in Carthage, Tennessee.

The Carthage Courier announced Monday that the family of Hershel and Geraldine Lake will be handing the paper's ownership to Gore, and that an agreement and ownership transfer will be finalized in the coming weeks.

Carthage is roughly 60 miles east of Nashville.

20 YEARS LATER, AL GORE AND HIS DIRECTOR DEFEND THEIR CONTROVERSIAL CLIMATE MOVIE 'AN INCONVENIENT TRUTH'

Former Vice President Al Gore has become a vocal climate change advocate in recent years. (Matthias Nareyek/Getty Images for Paramount Pictures)

"I’m so grateful to the Lake family for their decades of leadership in supporting independent news here in Smith County," Gore said in a statement. "Having spent my early years as a military reporter in Vietnam and later at the Tennessean, I am a firm believer that a free, independent local press is irreplaceable for the enduring health of our community. When my hometown paper came up for sale, I saw an opportunity to help preserve the Courier as an independent voice for Carthage and Smith County."

"I look forward to supporting the Carthage Courier team, many of whom have served this community for decades, as they continue to provide vital information and serve this community for generations to come," he added.

AL GORE SAYS CLIMATE CHANGE SUPPORTERS ‘KEEP QUIET’ ABOUT THEIR BELIEFS FOR FEAR OF RETALIATION

The Lake family put the Courier up for sale this fall after 50 years of operating the 113-year-old paper. Geraldine Lake died on Nov. 1 at 84.

The Courier also announced that its longtime publisher, Scott Winfree, will transition into a part-time role, citing health issues, and that newspaper advertising director Roger Wells will step in as the Courier's new publisher going forward.

The paper assured readers that publication will continue during the ownership transition and that all current staff will be retained.

CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS

Before buying The Carthage Courier, Gore previously served a reporter for The Tennessean and launched Current TV in 2005.  (Paul Marotta/Getty Images)

This isn't Gore's first foray into media. The former VP previously launched Current TV in 2005, which featured programs hosted by various media and political figures including Keith Olbermann, Joy Behar, Gavin Newsom, Jennifer Granholm and Eliot Spitzer.

The network was sold to Al Jazeera in 2013.

Before entering politics, Gore worked as a military journalist in the U.S. Army, serving during the Vietnam War, and later worked as an investigative reporter for The Tennessean.

Joseph A. Wulfsohn is a media reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to joseph.wulfsohn@fox.com and on Twitter: @JosephWulfsohn.

Martha Firestone Ford, the owner and chair emeritus of the Detroit Lions, has died, the team announced. She was 101.

The team said Ford died surrounded by her family and loved ones.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Martha Firestone Ford stands on the sidelines before the Detroit Lions game against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, Oct. 17, 2021, at Ford Field. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

Ford and her husband, William Clay Ford, received full control of the team in 1963 and she assumed full control of the Lions after he died in 2014. Ford transitioned to emeritus in 2020.

"In her most recent role as Owner/Chair Emeritus, Mrs. Ford supported her four children – Principal Owner/Chair Sheila Ford Hamp, Owner/Vice Chair Martha Ford Morse, Owner/Vice Chair William Clay Ford Jr., and Owner/Vice Chair Elizabeth Ford Kontulis – as they assumed leadership responsibilities within the family franchise," the team said in its obituary.

"Today the Ford family proudly carries forward the legacy established by Mr. and Mrs. Ford, preserving the values, love, and passion that have shaped a family tradition spanning multiple generations."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Detroit Lions owner Martha Firestone Ford leaves the field after training camp at the Allen Park facility on Wednesday, July 28, 2021. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

The Lions highlighted Ford’s charity work in the community. She backed the Detroit Lions Inspire Change initiative and held top positions in Merrill Palmer Skillman Institute, University Liggett School, Children's Home of Detroit and Edsel and Eleanor Ford House. She was also the founding member of the Henry Ford Maplegrove Center.

"It is with heavy hearts that we acknowledge the passing of Mattha Firestone Ford," the team sid in a statement. "Mrs. Ford inspired us all as a pillar of the Detroit community and the passionate matriarch of the Detroit Lions football team.

"She will always be remembered for her fierce loyalty to her family, her community and the city of Detroit."

Ford was a part of an exclusive club of pioneering businesswomen in the NFL as well.

She was among the group of NFL matriarchs that included the Chicago Bears’ Virginia Halas McCaskey, Pittsburgh Steelers’ Patricia Rooney and Kansas City Chiefs’ Norma Hunt.

Detroit Lions owner Martha Firestone Ford stands with new Executive Vice President and General Manager Bob Quinn at the Allen Park practice facility on Jan. 11, 2016. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

"Her presence on our sideline, in our building, and in our community will be greatly missed. We wish the entire Ford and Firestone families peace in this time of mourning."

articles.title: WHO chief urges end to US fuel blockade on Cuba
articles.excerpt:
World Health ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus has called for the lifting of a US fuel blockade on Cuba, as shortages dent the island’s once vaunted healthcare system.

Tedros warn...
articles.body_text:
World Health ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus has called for the lifting of a US fuel blockade on Cuba, as shortages dent the island’s once vaunted healthcare system.

Tedros warned that the sanctions were endangering the lives of children on Tuesday, during a ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠visit to Cuba that included tours of several healthcare facilities in Havana.

“The intensification ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠of fuel restrictions and sanctions is causing direct harm to the Cuban people, especially the most vulnerable,” Tedros said.

During his three-day visit, the United Nations health agency’s top official said his organisation would contribute $2m to help strengthen Cuba’s ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌national immunisation programme and provide essential medical equipment to healthcare facilities.

The UN has repeatedly warned of a growing humanitarian crisis on the island, calling the US blockade a violation of international law and the human rights of all Cubans.

Cuba’s government says the measures ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠led to daily power outages lasting 20 hours ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠or more, critical shortages of medicines and surgical supplies, and a decline in health indicators, such as infant mortality rates.

Tedros met with Cuba’s President Miguel Diaz-Canel on Tuesday to discuss the country’s health needs.

“We agreed on the need to prioritise essential health services and time-sensitive interventions, particularly for children,” Tedros wrote in a post on X.

“Fuel restrictions and sanctions affecting the purchase of medical products are severely impacting the health system that Cuban doctors have built over decades.”

Tedros said during a news conference that Cuba’s life expectancy had fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 years in 2025, the first decline since records began in 1950.

The 2025 figures predate the imposition by the administration of US President Donald Trump of a fuel blockade and stiff sanctions against a ‌number of Cuban officials and entities in January.

Washington argues the energy blockade is intended to push for ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠political change on the island and says that exports of food and medicine are subject ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠to legal exemptions.

An annual non-binding resolution calling for an end to a US embargo on the island has ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌passed ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌in favour of Cuba in the UN General Assembly by wide margins every year since 1992.

articles.title: Florida AG calls for doctor to lose medical license over 149 alleged illegal abortions
articles.excerpt:
Florida AG James Uthmeier calls for revoking Dr. Sylvester Braithwaite’s medical license, citing at least 149 alleged illegal abortions. (Credit: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier)

Florida Atto...
articles.body_text:
Florida AG James Uthmeier calls for revoking Dr. Sylvester Braithwaite’s medical license, citing at least 149 alleged illegal abortions. (Credit: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier)

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier is pushing to strip a North Miami Beach doctor of his medical license over at least 149 suspected illegal abortions, a number he says could rise to 180 as the investigation continues.

Uthmeier said in a video posted by his office on X that preliminary reports from state health officials indicate Dr. Sylvester Braithwaite allegedly performed the procedures between June 2024 and September 2026.

He said some may have been late-term abortions and called on the Florida Board of Medicine to revoke Braithwaite’s license.

DEM GOV MAURA HEALEY SIGNS SWEEPING MASSACHUSETTS BILL ALLOWING ABORTIONS UP TO BIRTH

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier during a news conference. He is calling for a Miami doctor to lose his medical license over alleged illegal abortions. (Joe Burbank/Orlando Sentinel/Tribune News Service via Getty Images, File)

"A medical license is not a license to break the law," Uthmeier said.

Uthmeier cited Florida’s Heartbeat Protection Act and said none of the cases fell under the exceptions he outlined for medical emergencies or victims of rape, incest or human trafficking. He said each alleged violation amounts to a third-degree felony.

"My office is investigating this conduct, and we will follow the facts wherever they lead," Uthmeier said. "And we will prosecute doctors who ignore our laws."

Noah Brandt, executive vice president of the anti-abortion group Live Action, told Fox News Digital that Braithwaite should lose his medical license for good and face prosecution if investigators confirm the allegations.

"If these allegations are true, at least 149 innocent preborn children were killed in direct violation of Florida law, and each of those children deserves justice," Brandt said. "The killing of innocent human beings, including through abortion, should be illegal, and the fundamental human rights of every person, born and preborn, must be protected under the law."

‘YOU’RE FIRED’: NEARLY 40 PRO-LIFE GROUPS URGE TRUMP ADMIN TO CUT OFF PLANNED PARENTHOOD FUNDS

Women & Teens Healthcare in North Miami Beach, Fla., where Dr. Sylvester Braithwaite serves as medical director, according to his professional biography. (Google Maps)

Brandt said Braithwaite should be "prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law" if the allegations are proven.

He also praised Uthmeier for "his commitment to enforcing Florida’s pro-life laws and setting an example for attorneys general across the country."

Florida state Rep. Taylor Yarkosky backed Uthmeier in a reply on X, calling the alleged conduct "the Devil at work" and thanking the attorney general "for upholding the law in Florida, and mostly for protecting the lives of the unborn!"

Uthmeier did not say whether any charges had been filed or how far along the pregnancies were in the cases he described as potentially late-term.

A woman hands a pamphlet to a person outside of Women & Teens Healthcare, a clinic that provides abortion services in North Miami Beach, Fla. (Josh Ritchie for The Washington Post via Getty Images, File)

Braithwaite is a board-certified obstetrician and gynecologist who serves as medical director of Women & Teens Healthcare in North Miami Beach, according to his professional biography.

The Florida Department of Health lists his medical license as active and confirms his certification in obstetrics and gynecology.

Fox News Digital reached out to Braithwaite’s office for comment.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

articles.title: Piker backs idea to sell Trump on Medicare-for-all by calling it 'Trumpcare'
articles.excerpt:
Left-wing streamer Hasan Piker praised Abdul El-Sayed's suggestion that Democrats can get President Trump to support Medicare-for-all by calling it ‘Trumpcare.’

Left-wing influencer Hasan Piker expre...
articles.body_text:
Left-wing streamer Hasan Piker praised Abdul El-Sayed's suggestion that Democrats can get President Trump to support Medicare-for-all by calling it ‘Trumpcare.’

Left-wing influencer Hasan Piker expressed support for Michigan Democratic Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed’s plan to get President Donald Trump to support Medicare-for-all by appealing to his ego and calling it "Trumpcare."

Speaking to liberal tech podcaster Kara Swisher on Monday, Piker lamented enduring the last two years of Trump’s term.

"He's [Trump's] so bad at everything," Piker said. "He's so incompetent, and all he cares about is enriching himself and his family. So, I don't know. I don't know where we go from here."

"We go to Trumpcare," Swisher quipped. "We go to Trumpcare for Medicare-for-all. That's what we're going to call it. That's the situation. Do you object to what El-Sayed said?"

HASAN PIKER DECLARES 'WOKE IS BACK,' FANTASIZES ABOUT PUTTING DONALD TRUMP IN PRISON

Twitch streamer Hasan Piker said he loves El-Sayed's suggestion that Medicare-for-all be labeled "Trumpcare" to appeal to the president's ego. (Florencia Tan Jun/Web Summit via Sportsfile via Getty Images)

"No, I love it. I've been saying that for years," Piker replied. "Literally, I've been presenting this as a joke for, like, the last decade. I was like, ‘Look, you tell Donald Trump, what does Donald Trump love more than anything else?’ Undermining Obama's legacy. He loves his name.

"He loves putting his name on stuff, and he loves undermining Obama's legacy. You pitch it to him as such. You say, ‘Look, Obamacare is done. This is better. Trumpcare is better. More comprehensive. Everyone will love you. You will be remembered as a legend."

Earlier this month, El-Sayed posted a 16-second video urging the president to embrace Medicare-for-all and call it "Trumpcare."

UNEARTHED AUDIO EXPOSES STUNNING EL-SAYED ADMISSION ABOUT HIS HEALTHCARE PITCH

Abdul El-Sayed talks poolside with streamer Hasan Piker at a party for content creators supporting his campaign Aug. 3, 2026, in Detroit. (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

"Donald. Habibi. Midterms were rough. I get it," El-Sayed said in the video posted Nov. 17, addressing Trump with the Arabic term "habibi," commonly translated as "my dear" or "my beloved."

"Trumpcare-for-all. It's really popular. People really want healthcare. You can put your name all over it."

The video featured a mock "Trumpcare" card and an AI-generated image depicting Trump as Jesus Christ, which El-Sayed, a Muslim, referenced while urging the president to embrace socialized, taxpayer-funded healthcare.

"Donald, this is your chance to heal the sick (like in that one AI image. You know the one)," El-Sayed said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed appeared to joke about Trump as he suggested the president adopt Medicare-for-all as Trumpcare. (Getty Images)

The White House responded at the time by blasting the pitch, warning that the Medicare-for-all proposal would threaten Americans' existing health coverage.

"The radical Democrats’ socialist proposal for a government takeover of healthcare should really be called ‘Medicare-for-none’ as it destroys access to the life-saving care Americans rely on daily," White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster told Fox News Digital.

Theo Wold, a former White House deputy assistant for domestic policy during Trump's first term, spoke to Fox News Digital about the Piker's comments.

"Democrats just won historic victories, but they understand that they still have two years in which anything that’s going to get done has to go through Trump," he said.

"Their simplistic assessment of Trump isn’t accurate and won’t work, but Republicans should read between the lines and forget stupid ideas like amnesty. Don’t give Democrats anything during these two years unless it’s a policy Republicans (and more importantly, Republican voters) actually want."

Republican consultant Mary Marslender reacted to Piker's commentary as well.

"Hasan Piker and his cronies are attempting to sell a government takeover of healthcare that would destroy the private innovation patients actually need," she wrote.

"Trump has proven he only promotes policies that are good for our country, not policies that appeal to ego. He understands that Medicare-for-all would threaten access to breakthrough treatments, raise prices, limit choices, and deny Americans access to care."

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House and did not receive an immediate reply.

Fox News’ Jasmine Baehr contributed to this report.

Alexander Hall is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to Alexander.hall@fox.com.

Bruce Pearl reacts to the SEC sending a strong message to LSU, with the chance the program is kicked from the conference.

LSU’s first regular season under Lane Kiffin wraps up on Saturday when the Tigers face Arkansas in Fayetteville.

A football season that could end with no more than seven wins, amid controversy over the eligibility of former NFL players, has fallen well short of what LSU likely hoped for. But an even greater disappointment could be looming in Baton Rouge.

According to an amended complaint filed Monday in federal court in Alabama, the SEC has threatened to put LSU’s possible expulsion from the conference to a vote. Commissioner Greg Sankey has scheduled another special meeting for Dec. 3, "to consider the termination of LSU's membership in the SEC."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey speaks to the press during SEC Football Kickoff Media Day at the Tampa Marriott in Tampa, Fla., on July 20, 2026. (Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images)

If the vote takes place, LSU’s fate would rest with the conference’s chancellors and presidents.

Whether the school broke the conference's policies on professionalism on former NFL players has been called into question. However, LSU’s issues extend to its basketball program, where former NBA players have been added to the roster.

Former St. John’s player RJ Luis Jr. appeared in preseason games with the Boston Celtics last season. He played in one game for the Tigers, scoring 11 points ina a 79-67 Tigers win over Louisiana-Monroe last Wednesday. Shortly after the game, LSU President Wade Rousse said he told Tigers basketball coach Will Wade should not take the court in future games.

LSU POKED THE SEC BEAR, THEN FOLDED: RJ LUIS BENCHED AFTER CONFERENCE LEADERS DISCUSSED EXPULSION OR BOYCOTT

In an affidavit, Sankey said the conference will consider expelling LSU regardless of whether Luis remains sidelined.

NFL rules analyst Terry McAulay weighed in and offered a blunt criticism of his alma mater’s coaching decisions and alleged conference-rule violations. "LSU is my alma mater. I’ve had no relationship with them other than the normal affinity for one’s alma mater for decades," McAulay wrote in a post on X retweeting a statement from the SEC.

Referee Terry McAulay makes a call during the first quarter of a preseason game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Aug. 20, 2016 at EverBank Field in Jacksonville, Florida. (Joel Auerbach/Getty Images)

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Their choice of head coaches in major sports and their recent behavior has been deeply embarrassing and they deserve whatever consequence may ensue."

The SEC defended its authority to govern its member schools and enforce its rules.

SEC ACCUSES LSU OF DEFYING ITS RULES AS WILL WADE’S BASKETBALL ROSTER ADDS FUEL TO A BURNING FIRE

"The lawsuit seeks to protect the Conference’s ability to govern itself and to enforce the rules and policies its member universities have voluntarily adopted," the statement from the conference read. "The Conference maintains its right to associate only with institutions that meet its established standards and expectations of membership and that demonstrate appropriate institutional control of their athletics programs. Monday’s filing advances the Conference’s obligation to defend its governance framework and the shared interests of its member universities."

A detailed view of the SEC logo painted on the field after a game between the LSU Tigers and the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, Louisiana on Oct. 17, 2026. (Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images)

The SEC was founded in 1932, with LSU being one of the conference's charter members.

The SEC first filed the lawsuit in September after LSU and Kiffin entertained adding former NFL players who had prevailed in similar eligibility court cases. The league held similar meetings that month, but LSU was not hit with any penalties at that time.

Under SEC bylaws, a school’s membership may be terminated involuntarily if at least two-thirds of the conference CEOs vote to do so at a meeting.

Chantz Martin is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

The selection committee has officially traded credibility for drama, ranking manufactured television narratives instead of actual on-field resumes.

This week's iteration of the College Football Playoff selection committee Top 25 poll is out, and after a wild week in the Big Ten Conference, there are some major changes near the top of the rankings.

The Alabama Crimson Tide, a contentious pick in recent weeks at No. 3, saw their strength of schedule and resume take a step back as their conference wins either all lost or beat an FCS team. That loss came on the road and after the Bruins saw second-string quarterback Ty Dieffenbach go down with a lower body injury in overtime. Leading to Madden Iamaleava's disastrous mistake in the second overtime period. Which made the Bruins' status heading into a massive rivalry game against USC on Saturday one of the major storylines of the week.

Head coach Curt Cignetti has been vocal in his criticism of the selection committee and their choices, for good reason, but the defending national champs finally got burned after weeks of playing with fire. The Hoosiers suffered a shocking defeat on the road against the Washington Huskies, their second of the season. And with a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game no longer a guarantee, their position in the rankings suddenly became a major talking point for their program and the conference.

Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti looks on during the Indiana Hoosiers versus the Miami Hurricanes College Football Playoff National Championship Game Presented by AT&T on Jan. 19, 2026, at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida. (David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

What about Wake Forest? The Demon Deacons have steamrolled their way through the ACC, outside a 33-20 loss to Miami, beating Stanford by 54 points, NC State by 24, California by 34, Virginia by 44, SMU by 42, and Georgia Tech by 21. Would they finally move their way up into the top 10?

BYU too, has struggled after their win over Notre Dame, escaping in triple overtime on the road against the Kansas Jayhawks. Would their seeming vulnerability in recent weeks cost them in the committee's eyes?

What about Tennessee? The Volunteers, despite their similar resume to Alabama and a head-to-head win, have sat behind the Tide in the rankings. Would the committee finally move them up? This week, they finally did.

Alabama fell three spots to No. 6, while Tennessee surged up four spots to No. 5. Wake Forest also finally got the boost they've been waiting for, leapfrogging UCLA and BYU to move to No. 8. Indiana fell a whopping six spots after losing to a now-ranked UW team on the road, and UCLA crashed to No. 9, meaning just one Big Ten team currently sits in the 12-team field. Dropped out: Kentucky (was #16), Boise State (was #17), South Carolina (was #21)

If there's one thing for certain, it's that Georgia's already clinched their spot in the 12-team field, regardless of how the rest of the season plays out. Kirby Smart's team has their signature win over Alabama and should blow out an awful Georgia Tech team on Saturday, making the SEC conference championship game all but a formality.

Georgia Bulldogs head coach Kirby Smart motions during the first half against the Florida Gators at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Ga., on Oct. 31, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

But rivalry weekend should lead to plenty of intrigue, with UCLA-USC, Washington-Oregon, Cincinnati-BYU, Tennessee-Vanderbilt all carrying playoff implications. And Auburn hoping to pull off its second shocking upset of the season against Alabama.

As always, college football is anything but boring.

articles.title: Israel’s Eisenkot secures first coalition partner in bid to form government
articles.excerpt:
Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party has announced an agreement to unite with a right-wing opposition party in a bid to form the next Israeli government following October’s elections.

The Yashar party said o...
articles.body_text:
Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party has announced an agreement to unite with a right-wing opposition party in a bid to form the next Israeli government following October’s elections.

The Yashar party said on Tuesday that it agreed to sign a coalition pact with Israel’s Our Home party after a meeting with its leader Avigdor Lieberman, the first alliance of its kind since the election.

After no party managed to secure a 61-seat majority, Israel’s parliament was sworn in on November 10 without a new government.

President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming ⁠a government, while Benjamin Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister despite the October 27 election stripping Netanyahu of his majority.

Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government under a 28-day mandate, though he could ask for a 14-day extension. If Eisenkot fails, Netanyahu would have an opportunity to do so. If no one is able to form a government, another election will be held next year.

The agreement between Eisenkot, whose party won 21 parliament seats, and Lieberman, whose party won seven, was unforeseen since Lieberman has been vocal about his opposition to forming a government with support from Arab parties as well as to a unity government with Netanyahu.

Lieberman had once served as foreign minister under a previous Netanyahu government but has since become a strong critic.

Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud’s alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties outperformed election expectations but still lost its majority. It now holds 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats.

Eisenkot’s centre-right Yashar party and patchwork coalition partners, including Lieberman, hold just 48 seats. But they have potential allies in the parties representing Israel’s Arab minority, which hold 19 seats and ⁠are aligned with Eisenkot in their vehement opposition to Netanyahu.

Talks are also ongoing between Eisenkot, some of his “change bloc” partners and Likud on forming a unity government.

The left-wing Democrats party, which won eight parliament seats, separately said it was suspending talks with Eisenkot after the Yashar party leader’s talks with Netanyahu’s Likud on a possible unity government.

Yair Golan, head of the Democrats, said he prefers a government without Netanyahu but with Arab parties.

articles.title: California prosecutors, victim advocates challenge Newsom's mass death sentence commutation
articles.excerpt: Victim advocates and California prosecutors are pushing back against Gov. Gavin Newsom’s blanket commutation of all 548 death row sentences, arguing the move overrides the will of voters, bypasses ind...
articles.body_text:
Victim advocates and California prosecutors are pushing back against Gov. Gavin Newsom’s blanket commutation of all 548 death row sentences, arguing the move overrides the will of voters, bypasses individual case reviews and could eventually open a legal pathway to freedom for convicted killers.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom justified his blanket commutation of 548 death sentences to life without parole by arguing that reviewing cases individually would create "two classes of murder victims," a rationale victims' advocates and at least one district attorney called "morally offensive. "

Modoc County District Attorney Nina Salarno said Newsom's sweeping action denied the loved ones of murder victims any voice in the clemency process.

"I found it really offensive as a victim myself, and [for] my other victims," Salarno told Fox News Digital from Washington, D. C., where she and fellow advocates met with President Donald Trump this week. "There should be individual scrutiny. The individual victims should have a voice. And that's what he has avoided by doing a blanket commutation."

CALIFORNIA PROSECUTORS SLAM NEWSOM'S DEATH ROW COMMUTATIONS, ACCUSE GOVERNOR OF PUTTING 'POLITICS OVER PEOPLE'

Gov. Gavin Newsom speaks on March 26, 2025, in Los Angeles. (Frazer Harrison/WireImage)

"The blanket commutation on a moral level as a victim I find very offensive, but I find the whole thing offensive to our entire rule of law," she added.

Topo Padilla, president of Crime Victims United, a nonprofit that advocates for stricter laws against violent offenders, noted that California voters have repeatedly upheld the death penalty at the ballot box, including approving a 2016 measure aimed at speeding up executions.

"Here's a guy who throws rocks about kings and protests throughout the streets," Padilla said, referring to Newsom's past criticisms of Trump. "I will promise you, this is a move that is looked at and viewed as a king. He is trampling on the voters."

On Monday, Trump vowed to direct the Justice Department to seek the death penalty for child murderers and expedite federal executions as victims’ relatives spoke out at the Justice Department against Newsom's order.

Lieutenant Sam Robinson, a public information officer at San Quentin State Prison, knocks on the door to the East Block for condemned prisoners during a media tour of California's Death Row in San Quentin, Calif., on Dec. 29, 2015. (Stephen Lam/Reuters)

SLAIN FIREFIGHTER'S MOTHER PLEADS WITH TRUMP TO INTERVENE AFTER NEWSOM STOPS KILLER'S DEATH SENTENCE

"Gavin Newsom and the radical left look at these heinous acts, and their sympathy is not for the children and their parents, but for the monsters who extinguished innocent young lives," Trump said. "He stood with the murderers and child slayers."

Justice for crime victims shouldn't be a partisan issue, Padilla said.

"Whether you're a Democrat or a Republican, you take politics out of this," he said. "The president of the United States stood up and sounded the alarm. And I hope the country hears it."

Newsom's office referred Fox News Digital to news release from Monday featuring victims and survivors who support his decision.

President Donald Trump approaches, Gloria Vega, daughter of murdered Palm Springs police officer Jose "Gil" Vega, at the Department of Justice in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 23, 2026, as he criticizes California Gov. Gavin Newsom over his decision to commute the death sentences of 548 prisoners. (Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters)

GAVIN NEWSOM WIPES OUT CALIFORNIA'S DEATH ROW IN HISTORIC MASS COMMUTATION

"As a member of the clergy, I believe that all life is sacred. I also believe in the possibility of redemption. Because of this, I oppose the death penalty," said Rabbi Suzanne Singer, the sister of Michele Reiner and sister-in-law of famed film director Rob Reiner, who were both stabbed to death in December 2025 inside their Los Angeles home.

"As a civilized nation, it is barbaric that we still subject people to die at the hands of the state. I am so grateful to Governor Newsom for commuting the death sentences that have been imposed in our state. This is true proof of his moral character."

On Nov. 16, a coalition of roughly 30 county district attorneys, law enforcement groups, victims' rights advocates and grieving families filed a petition with the California Supreme Court seeking to halt Newsom's commutations.

MICHAEL RUIZ: DA IDENTIFIES 49 LOCAL KILLERS SLATED FOR NEWSOM'S DEATH ROW CLEMENCY — AND THEIR CRIMES

Salarno argued that the governor's move disrespects the jurors and judges who endured months-long capital trials. Even though California has not carried out an execution since 2006, Padilla noted that the death sentence itself provides essential legal validation and finality for grieving families, a loss he knows firsthand.

"The fact of the matter is the law is the law," Padilla said. "It's like changing the innings in a baseball game, changing from nine to seven retroactively, going back [and] going, 'I know you won that game, but we're going to make it seven innings and now you lost.'"

CALIFORNIA DA SAYS GAVIN NEWSOM'S 'CRUEL' DEATH ROW CLEMENCY STABS CRIME VICTIMS 'IN THE HEART'

The fight is also deeply personal for Salarno, whose older sister, Catina Rose Salarno, was murdered in 1979 on her first day at the University of the Pacific by her former high school boyfriend, Steven Burns. Following the tragedy, Salarno's mother, Harriet, founded Crime Victims United.

"Look, my sister's never coming back, and I understand that," Padilla added. "But I have to accept that she was murdered, like these families have to accept that their loved ones were. And we have to trust the justice system. And now it's been taken away from them. And that's where I think the real issue comes."

Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

articles.title: Poll finds US voters want government to end Iran war regardless of terms
articles.excerpt:
A new poll has found that a majority of voters in the United States want an end to the US-Israel war on Iran immediately, even if it means accepting less favourable conditions.

Overall, 55 percent of...
articles.body_text:
A new poll has found that a majority of voters in the United States want an end to the US-Israel war on Iran immediately, even if it means accepting less favourable conditions.

Overall, 55 percent of those surveyed agreed with an “end to the war now, regardless of the terms”.

That number was even higher among Democrats and independents, who agreed with the statement at a rate of 80 percent and 59 percent, respectively. About 25 percent of Republicans said the same.

A majority of Democratic voters also supported steps to pressure the administration of President Donald Trump to stop the conflict.

Fifty-three percent of party members said they would favour Congress withholding funding for military operations, and 51 percent would back an “an Iran war-funding cutoff” in upcoming budget negotiations, even if the manoeuvre risked a government shutdown.

The numbers were published on Tuesday as part of the latest Critical Issues Poll, released by the University of Maryland and the research firm Ipsos.

Shibley Telhami, the poll’s principal investigator, said he was surprised by the level of support for ending the war, regardless of the terms.

“We knew that people were strongly opposed to this war and wanted it to end,” he told Al Jazeera in a phone call. “What we were less sure of is what they would be willing to accept to achieve this.”

The survey asked 1,022 US adults about their perspectives on the war.

In one question, they were tasked with assessing with three options: whether to end the conflict immediately, escalate militarily, or continue on the current path in order to extract concessions from Iran.

Just 21 percent of all respondents favoured the current path, and 18 percent supported escalation.

“Clearly, the public mood is to end it now, whatever it takes,” said Telhami.

Voters also appear sceptical about the US government’s arguments in favour of the war, which include dismantling Iran’s nuclear programme.

The Critical Issues Poll found that only 28 percent of those surveyed believed that the war had left Iran in “worse position” to develop nuclear weapons.

While the US has long voiced concerned that Iran could pursue nuclear arms, intelligence assessments have not found evidence that Tehran has authorised such a step since abandoning its nuclear weapons programme in 2003.

The Strait of Hormuz has also emerged as a key issue, with Iran closing the waterway to commercial traffic early in the war. The Trump administration has responded with a naval blockade in the strait.

Some 20 percent of the world’s oil supply passes through the maritime artery, and fuel prices have spiked as a result of the war.

About 35 percent of respondents in Tuesday’s poll said that they believe Iran is now in control of the strait, while just 12.7 percent said the US is in control.

The poll comes as the Democratic Party is debating how far it should go to end the unpopular war.

In the recent midterm elections, backlash against the war — and as well as related issues like rising fuel prices — contributed to big gains for the Democratic Party.

Trump’s Republican Party, meanwhile, suffered one of its most bruising setbacks in modern US history, losing control of both chambers of Congress.

Members of the Democratic Party’s anti-war left have pointed to the results as proof that voters want an end to the war and an end to US support for Israel.

But that position has brought them into conflict with members of the party’s more hawkish establishment wing.

While leaders such as Representative Hakeem Jeffries and Senator Chuck Schumer have both expressed support for ending the war, they have yet to commit to aggressive strategies to reach that goal.

That includes potentially cutting off funding for military operations against Iran, or using an upcoming funding battle in December to demand that the White House end the war.

“A lot of Democratic figures are dismissing the intensity of public feeling on this issue,” said Telhami. “If they don’t adapt, they will be left behind.”

He added that progressive figures such as Senator Bernie Sanders and Senator Chris Van Hollen have been among those pressing for a more assertive stance.

Van Hollen, who is challenging Schumer to lead the Democratic majority in the US Senate, has used the war to portray the party’s moderate leadership as out of step with voters.

The poll found that Democratic voters prefer Van Hollen over Schumer by a ratio of nearly three to one.

articles.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
articles.excerpt:
Defence lawyer Brian Heberlig makes closing arguments at the Huawei Technologies trial at Brooklyn federal court on November 17.

Huawei has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and ...
articles.body_text:
Defence lawyer Brian Heberlig makes closing arguments at the Huawei Technologies trial at Brooklyn federal court on November 17.

Huawei has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but not guilty of the more serious overarching racketeering charge in a landmark case in the US.

In a two-month trial, prosecutors accused the Chinese technology and telecommunications giant of lying, cheating and stealing to gain any competitive advantage.

Huawei's defence team argued that prosecutors had decided Huawei was a criminal organisation and built its case from there, but the firm's success was due to its own innovation.

In a statement, Huawei said the racketeering acquittal "confirms that these allegations lack factual basis and vindicates our consistent position over the past eight years".

Jurors in a Brooklyn court found Huawei guilty of 10 out of 12 counts, which included conspiracy to violate US sanctions.

However, the jury declined to convict Huawei of the racketeering conspiracy charge, which required members to find the firm acted like a criminal enterprise.

Federal prosecutors first announced the charges against Huawei in 2019, after the dramatic arrest in late 2018 of senior executive Meng Wanzhou in Canada.

Meng, also known as Cathy Meng, was held for three years in Canada before she was released to return to China through a deal with US prosecutors.

During closing arguments last week, assistant US attorney Meredith Arfa told jurors Huawei spent 20 years doing whatever it took to expand its business, including lying to banks about its business dealings in Iran and stealing technology secrets from rival firms to ensure it had a competitive edge.

"For decades, Huawei and three of its subsidiaries conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft," US Attorney General Todd Blanche said in statement, external.

"Thanks to the work of the FBI and our federal prosecutors, those who engaged in these criminal activities will be held accountable."

However, defence attorney Brian Heberlig said it was by dint of hard work that Huawei's business had expanded with operations in 170 countries and more than 200,000 staff.

Following the verdict, Heberlig told the BBC that Huawei was gratified that the jury had rejected the racketeering charge.

"The RICO [Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act] count that alleged that Huawei was a corrupt organisation, with a corporate culture and policy of committing crime. That was, in our view, a significant overreach, and the jury soundly rejected it," he said.

"Of course, we have mixed emotions about the rest of the verdict ... [we] thought that Huawei was deserving of acquittals across the board."

Sentencing is planned for September 2027. Heberlig said there will be "significant advocacy" to achieve the lowest sentence possible. Following that, he said he fully expects Huawei to appeal.

"If I know Huawei, that fight will continue, and the company's not going to rest until it's pursued every last argument it can through appeal, and hopefully, ultimately toward vindication," he said.

articles.body_text:
Federal immigration officers arrested Ariel Antonio Velasquez-Morales in East Boston after a brief foot chase. The arrest came days after he claimed a $1 million Massachusetts State Lottery prize.

A man who smiled for a Massachusetts State Lottery photo with a $1 million check was arrested by federal immigration officers days later after a brief foot chase in East Boston.

Three ICE sources told Fox News that Ariel Antonio Velasquez-Morales, an illegal immigrant from El Salvador, ran when officers moved in to arrest him early Tuesday but was quickly caught.

Multiple officers’ body cameras captured the encounter, the sources said.

ICE ARRESTS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED OF RAPE, MULTIPLE SEX CRIMES AFTER RELEASE FROM MARYLAND JAIL

Ariel Antonio Velasquez-Morales holds a ceremonial $1 million check dated Nov. 18, 2026. The Massachusetts State Lottery said he bought the winning ticket at a market in East Boston. (Massachusetts State Lottery via Facebook)

Velasquez-Morales had been wanted by ICE under a final deportation order issued in April 2014, the sources said.

He crossed the U.S. border illegally near Roma, Texas, in 2013, according to the sources.

MASSACHUSETTS SUES TRUMP ADMIN TO STOP ICE'S COURTHOUSE ARRESTS: 'UNNECESSARY FEAR'

Velasquez-Morales had been wanted by ICE under a final deportation order issued in April 2014. (Dept. of Homeland Security/ICE, File)

The Massachusetts State Lottery awarded Velasquez-Morales the $1 million prize Nov. 18, and posted a photo on Facebook three days later showing him holding the oversized check.

The lottery said he bought The Lottery's winning "$2,000,000 50X Cashword" $10 scratch ticket at a market in East Boston, the same neighborhood where ICE arrested him.

Ariel Antonio Velasquez-Morales is shown in ICE custody after his arrest in East Boston, Mass., on Tuesday, six days after he won a $1 million Massachusetts State Lottery prize. (ICE Boston)

The Massachusetts State Lottery says anyone 18 or older can buy a ticket from a licensed retailer. The governor appoints two members of the five-member commission that oversees the lottery.

Fox News Digital reached out to Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey’s office and the lottery for comment.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

articles.title: Coast Guard searching for 2 children, 4 adults after plane crashes off Mississippi coast
articles.excerpt:
The plane was reportedly heading from New Orleans to Fort Myers, Florida, when it went down southwest of Pascagoula with four adults and two children on board.

U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) rescue crews ar...
articles.body_text:
The plane was reportedly heading from New Orleans to Fort Myers, Florida, when it went down southwest of Pascagoula with four adults and two children on board.

U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) rescue crews are conducting a search operation off the Mississippi Gulf Coast Tuesday after a plane carrying six people went down.

In a post on X, the U.S. Coast Guard Heartland said the Cessna 210 Centurion aircraft went down 2 miles northeast of Horn Island.

"[USCG] rescue crews are searching for a downed Cessna 210 Centurion aircraft with 6 people, 2 mi NE of Horn Island, Mississippi, after [USCG] watchstanders in Mobile received a report from [the Federal Aviation Administration], Tuesday," the U.S. Coast Guard Heartland said.

BODY WASHED ASHORE IN OREGON IDENTIFIED AS FORMER CITY COUNCILOR MISSING SINCE SEPTEMBER PLANE CRASH

U.S. Coast Guard rescue crews are conducting a search operation off the Mississippi Gulf Coast Tuesday after a plane carrying six people went down. (Smith Collection/Gado/Getty Images)

A Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) spokesperson confirmed to Fox News Digital the plane went down southwest of Pascagoula, Mississippi, at about 3:30 p.m. local time.

"The number of people on board is unknown at this time," the spokesperson said. "The FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) will investigate. The NTSB will lead the investigation and provide any updates."

FLORIDA LEARJET CRASH 911 CALLERS REPORT HEARING ‘BOMB’ AS PLANE CARRYING YOUNG FAMILY PLUNGES NEAR BUSY ROAD

A Federal Aviation Administration spokesperson confirmed to Fox News Digital the plane went down southwest of Pascagoula, Miss., at about 3:30 p.m. local time. (iStock)

The plane was descending at 10,000 feet per minute when it crashed, prompting an active search for four adults and two children between the ages of 8 and 12, according to local outlets WDSU and WLOX, citing the USCG.

The aircraft was traveling from New Orleans Lakefront Airport to Page Field in Fort Myers, Florida, when it dropped off FAA radar around 3:45 p.m., WLOX reported.

FLORIDA PLANE CRASH VICTIMS IDENTIFIED AFTER 9 PEOPLE KILLED IN FIERY WRECK

The FAA confirmed it will investigate. (AP Photo/Seth Wenig, File)

By 5:40 p.m., Coast Guard crews told WLOX they had located several pieces of wreckage, including the cabin, a life raft and three life jackets, though none of the passengers had been found.

A multi-agency response is underway in the area, according to the outlet.

The U.S. Coast Guard and NTSB could not immediately be reached by Fox News Digital for comment.

Sophia Compton is a Writer at Fox News Digital. Sophia was previously a business reporter covering finance, energy and tourism and has experience as a TV news producer. She graduated with a journalism degree in 2021 from the University of Hawaii at Manoa. Story tips can be sent to sophia.compton@fox.com.
