articles.body_text:
Joe Kinsey joins Dan Dakich for this week's edition of Screencaps recap!

UCLA's undefeated season came to an end in Ann Arbor this weekend when they lost to Michigan 18-16 in a triple overtime game. The Bruins dropped from the AP No. 4-ranked team in the country down to the No. 10-ranked team following the loss.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

It's not the type of loss you want to have this time of year. You have to handle your business against your unranked opponents no matter who it is and where the game is played. They didn't do that.

UCLA Bruins cheerleaders perform in the second half of an NCAA football game between the UCLA Bruins and Michigan State Spartans at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, Calif., on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. (MediaNews Group via Getty Images)

Despite the loss, UCLA's Miss California crown-wearing cheerleader Sharlize True Trujillo hasn't lost the spotlight. She went viral a couple of weeks ago in an 18-second clip on social media alongside cheerleaders Hayleigh Liu and Quillan Cas.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Sharlize is the redhead who makes an appearance towards the end of the clip, which has now been viewed more than 30 million times.

Her resume as Miss California 2026 and as the Miss America third runner-up has kept the attention coming her way.

Miss California Sharlize True Trujillo walks in sportswear by Rebel Athletic during the Miss America Preliminary Competition at the Kravis Center in downtown West Palm Beach, Fla., on Sept. 2, 2026. Fifty-two delegates competed in fitness, evening gown and answered an onstage question during the night's event. Miss America 2027 will be crowned on Sept. 6. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

One of the more recent articles about her introduced her boyfriend. He's an actor by the name of Jackson Dollinger, reports the NY Post.

TCU'S MOST FAMOUS CHEERLEADER ON THE SIDELINE AS 'LANDMAN' FILMED DURING HORNED FROGS WIN

But that's not all the internet has dug up about her. Sharlize is more than a viral pageant-winning UCLA cheerleader. She comes from a family of cheerleaders and has an extensive highlight package of her own.

A highlight package that shows those couple of seconds of camera time weren't a fluke. Her sister, Shariah True Trujillo, is currently a Denver Broncos cheerleader.

OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Her mom, Shelly True, is a former Broncos cheerleader herself who has "3 Super Bowl wins under her belt," according to her dance academy's website.

She's also currently Denver's choreographer and assistant director for the cheerleading squad. That's just a taste of mom's resume too.

Miss California Sharlize True Trujillo attends the Miss America and Miss America Teen Pre-Gala Red Carpet event at The Palm Beach County Convention Center in West Palm Beach, Fla., on Sept. 4, 2026. Fifty-two Miss America delegates hail from the states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico. Miss America 2027 will be crowned on Sept. 6 and Miss America Teen on Sept. 5. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

That just goes to show that folks on social media have an eye for talent.

Sharlize True Trujillo was about as prepared as one can be when her viral moment came knocking. Congratulations to the entire family for helping out with that.

articles.title: DK Metcalf avoids NFL and club suspension from the Pittsburgh Steelers following his ejection from Sunday game
articles.excerpt: Daniel Jones was released by the Indianapolis Colts following their 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans. Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, and Kevin Wildes ask what’s going on with the Colts, and if Puka Nacu...
articles.body_text:
Daniel Jones was released by the Indianapolis Colts following their 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans. Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, and Kevin Wildes ask what’s going on with the Colts, and if Puka Nacua’s surgery means that the Los Angeles Rams will miss the playoffs.

DK Metcalf lost his composure but he didn't lose his ability to play for the Pittsburgh Steelers because the NFL has decided not to suspend the wide receiver despite him being ejected from Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

The league has instead opted to review Metcalf's conduct during the game and decide if fines are in order, a source confirmed.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

And the sound you hear coming from Western Pennsylvania is a sigh of relief.

Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf is ejected from the game during the fourth quarter at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia on Nov. 22, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

DK METCALF DISQUALIFIED FROM STEELERS GAME FOR UNSPORTSMANLIKE PENALTIES INCLUDING TRYING TO POKE OPPONENT'S EYES

Earlier on Monday, Metcalf talked with Mike McCarthy, and the Steelers' coach said he was comfortable with the receiver's accountability and approach and indicated there would be no team discipline that is public.

So Metcalf is in the clear to continue playing.

NEW NFL FINE SCHEDULE IS GOING TO A POINT SYSTEM THAT COULD LEAD TO SUSPENSIONS BUT ALSO REFUNDS

Metcalf was ejected from the Eagles game because NFL rules stipulate any player flagged twice for unsportsmanlike conduct related to taunting, abusive conduct or striking another player, is automatically disqualified.

Sunday's disqualification marks the third time in Metcalf's career he is removed from a game. Metcalf has been suspended by the NFL previously, that coming last year when he got into an argument with a fan.

So what happened in this game that led to Metcalf getting ejected?

"I can't remember," Metcalf told reporters on Monday after leaving the locker room on Sunday without speaking. "I just wish I had been there for my team."

Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf is escorted off the field after being disqualified during an NFL game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, Pa., on Nov. 22, 2026. The Eagles won 19-16. (Scott Serio/Cal Sport Media/Sipa USA via Reuters Connect)

Metcalf didn't think himself responsible for what happened and, hey, that's possible because in football it is sometimes the reacting party that gets caught instead of the offending party.

So, yeah, that's what Metcalf is going with.

"You got to ask the people that seemingly do that to me," Metcalf said when asked about his temper issues on the field.

It is fair to say something set off Metcalf and that something almost definitely was personified by Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean.

RAMS OL ALARIC JACKSON EXPECTING TWO-GAME SUSPENSION AFTER PUNCHING BILLS DEFENDER BRADLEY CHUBB

Cooper DeJean #33 of the Philadelphia Eagles jogs across the field before Super Bowl LIX against the Kansas City Chiefs at Caesars Superdome on February 09, 2025 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Emilee Chinn/Getty Images)

The two players got into a fracas in the third quarter on a play in which Metcalf was blocking DeJean. The blocking turned into something else when Metcalf grabbed DeJean by the collar, DeJean grabbed back, one pushed the other and then other players surrounded the pair.

It was basically a routine football fight and that's when Metcalf picked up his first flag. On the next offensive series for the Steelers, Metcalf was caught on camera poking at DeJean's facemask.

"I mean, we were just competing," DeJean said. "Things like that happen in football. It wasn't anything crazy. Just two guys going at it. He was trying to block me, I was trying to get him off me. And it carried over to whatever that was at the end."

Metcalf said nothing happened at the end. He denied poking DeJean at all.

"I wasn't trying to poke him in the eye," Metcalf said. "I was just telling him."

Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy looks on during the first quarter against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland, Ohio, on Oct. 1, 2026. (Gregory Shamus/Getty Images)

None of this washes away the question of Metcalf's long term prospects with the Steelers.

He is turning 29 years old next month and has three years remaining on his contract after this season at a cost of $90 million. But all of that money is unsecured by guaranteed money.

The Steelers must pay Metcalf a $6.5 million roster bonus on March 13 to retain his rights. The club can decline to pay the bonus and move on from the volatile player, and while that will carry nearly $70 million in dead cap money through 2029, it also comes with a salary cap savings of around $54 million over that time.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

So Metcalf's future is not secured with the Steelers by his contract and its salary cap implications. But is he worth keeping based on his talent?

Well, that talent is undeniable. He's 6-4 and fast as the wind. He should be great and has been in the past.

But that was around 2020-2023 with the Seattle Seahawks. The numbers – yards, receptions, touchdowns – have been in steady decline since 2024, including the past two seasons with the Steelers.

Metcalf's production, in other words, exposes him to being released in the offseason.

FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.

articles.title: US escalates sanctions on Iran, targets ‘shadow banking’ networks
articles.excerpt: The United States has launched another wave of sanctions against Iran under its Operation Economic Outcast, a move that comes shortly after US President Donald Trump threatened renewed military action...
articles.body_text:
The United States has launched another wave of sanctions against Iran under its Operation Economic Outcast, a move that comes shortly after US President Donald Trump threatened renewed military action next year.

The Department of the Treasury announced on Monday that it had targeted more than two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies, and key personnel with sanctions “in a sweeping effort to disrupt Iran’s global shadow banking networks”.

“Iran’s shadow banking system is the last financial lifeline of a bankrupt regime,” said US Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent.

The US Treasury claimed these entities help Iran “move billions of dollars through the international financial system to provide the regime access to foreign currency despite comprehensive sanctions”.

Bessent also vowed the “Treasury will continue dismantling these illicit networks until we have buried the head of the snake.”

The Central Bank of Iran oversees the designated entities, according to the statement.

The designated entities include an Iran-based company named “Rahbar Bazargani Nesim Baharan Qeshm Company (Nesim Baharan)”, which the Treasury claims worked closely with Iranian exchange houses and their front companies to facilitate transactions on behalf of Sarmayeh Bank’s Iranian clients, which include major Iranian petrochemical companies.

In addition, “Mina Fashki and Partners Exchange Company (Fashki Exchange) and Mellat Exchange Company” and a number of their owners and employees were designated.

The US claimed earlier this month that its sanctions campaign had pushed Iran’s rial to new lows and driven inflation to about 90 percent.

AP reported that Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran still hoped diplomacy could end its nine-month war with the US, while President Trump said Iran wanted a deal, but one that was not acceptable to him.

Fox News said Trump told its chief foreign correspondent that he was “inclined to order military strikes against Iran after the new year if the two countries fail to reach an agreement”.

The remarks came as diplomatic efforts continued to end a conflict that has destabilised the Middle East, disrupted shipping, driven up global energy prices, and drawn in countries across the region.

articles.title: $25 minimum wage backers frame midterms as 'blue-collar wave,' 'mandate' to raise pay
articles.excerpt:
One Fair Wage President Saru Jayaraman told Fox News Digital that the last election was a 'blue collar' mandate to act on affordability pressures.

Democrats' huge wins in the 2026 midterms represent ...
articles.body_text:
One Fair Wage President Saru Jayaraman told Fox News Digital that the last election was a 'blue collar' mandate to act on affordability pressures.

Democrats' huge wins in the 2026 midterms represent a "blue-collar wave" mandate for a $25 federal minimum wage, an advocate for the wage hike tells Fox News Digital.

One Fair Wage President Saru Jayaraman joined House Democrats and restaurant workers on Capitol Hill on Nov. 18 to urge the incoming 120th Congress "to answer the affordability election with a $25 living wage and to make the Living Wage for All Act a Day One priority."

"We're saying it's actually not a blue wave, it's a blue-collar wave. It's working people who didn't necessarily turn into Democrats but are demanding change so that they can meet the cost of living," Jayaraman said in an interview.

DEMOCRATS SEIZE ON MIDTERM WINS TO PUSH MASSIVE MINIMUM WAGE HIKES, BUT ECONOMISTS SEE TROUBLE AHEAD

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., speaks during a news conference on April 29, 2026, outside the U.S. Capitol about raising the federal minimum wage. (Tom Brenner/Getty Images)

"I don't care what their political affiliation [is], people are looking for help and change and relief because the cost of living is out of control," she added. "Nobody can live on the wages. Most people's pay doesn't meet the cost of living in America right now."

One Fair Wage co-leads the Living Wage for All coalition — a group of more than 100 organizations, including major teachers unions and progressive advocacy groups — pushing to more than triple the federal minimum wage, which has sat at $7.25 an hour since 2009.

SANDERS-AOC BACKED PROGRESSIVE DEBUTS FEDERAL $25 MINIMUM WAGE BILL WITH COALITION OF 100+ ORGANIZATIONS

Introduced in April by Rep. Delia Ramirez, D-Ill., and backed by 35 House cosponsors alongside a Senate companion from Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., the Living Wage for All Act would phase in a $25 hourly floor by 2031 for large employers and by 2038 for smaller businesses. The legislation would also eliminate the $2.13 federal subminimum wage for tipped workers and index future increases to the national median wage.

One of the bill's House co-leads is Rep. Analilia Mejia, D-N.J., a progressive who won an April special election before securing a full term on Nov. 3. Mejia, who was backed by Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., and Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., has campaigned on progressive priorities including Medicare for All, a wealth tax and abolishing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

'CRAZY': MODERATES FEAR DEM LEADERSHIP PROMISED FAR-LEFT REPARATIONS AND ICE DEMANDS IN TURN OF VOTES

The midterms that saw Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress was a "blue collar wave" that called for a federal $25 minimum wage, One Fair Wage President Saru Jayaraman told Fox News Digital on Monday. (Heather Khalifa/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Small-business advocates and restaurant industry groups have repeatedly warned that steep federal wage mandates could force employers to cut staff, raise menu prices or close altogether — particularly in rural states with significantly lower living costs than major coastal cities.

Rep. Everton Blair Jr., D-Ga., who attended the Nov. 18 Capitol Hill press conference, dismissed arguments that a $25 floor would hurt lower-cost states, arguing the rate should serve as a nationwide baseline.

PROGRESSIVES UNVEIL $25 MINIMUM WAGE PUSH TO SOLVE AFFORDABILITY CRISIS DESPITE ECONOMIST INFLATION WARNING

"We should be rallying around $25 at minimum, and it should be cost-adjusted for inflation, so that people can have a job that enables them to survive and thrive," Blair told Fox News Digital. He added that $25 an hour should be "the floor" and "should be higher in places with a higher cost of living."

While Blair acknowledged concerns that higher wage mandates could fuel inflation, he argued lawmakers must find a way to boost earnings while "keeping people afloat."

On Nov. 18, House Democrats and restaurant workers urged the incoming Congress "to answer the affordability election with a $25 living wage and to make the Living Wage for All Act a Day One priority." (Joshua Nelson / Fox News Digital)

AOC-BACKED $25 MINIMUM WAGE PLAN SOUNDS GREAT — BUT AT WHAT COST?

The renewed push comes after Democrats swept into majorities in both the House and Senate in the Nov. 3 midterms. However, when the new Congress convenes in January, Democrats will remain well short of the two-thirds supermajorities needed in each chamber to override a presidential veto — setting the stage for messaging bills aimed at forcing President Donald Trump to reject progressive economic proposals.

Still, Jayaraman insisted voters delivered an unmistakable verdict on wages as "people are overwhelmingly" demanding action quickly.

"There's a mandate from working people based on this election to deliver on raising wages closer to the cost of living," she said, adding, "Most people do not care about parties. Most people care about results. They want to see electeds deliver on the cost of living, and that means raising wages to the least you need to live anywhere in the U.S."

Joshua Q. Nelson is a reporter for Fox News Digital.

Joshua focuses on cultural trends, education, and public policy. He extensively covered reparations developments across the U.S., the Department of Education, and immigration issues.

Joining Fox News Digital in 2019, he previously graduated from Syracuse University's Maxwell School of Citizenship and Public Affairs and received the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton Public Policy Certificate.

Story tips can be sent to joshua.nelson@fox.com and Joshua can be followed on Instagram, Twitter and LinkedIn.

articles.title: US states sue SpaceX over Grok AI’s creation of child sexual abuse material
articles.excerpt: The US states of Virginia and Oregon have sued Elon Musk’s SpaceX, saying the business harmed consumers by avoiding safeguards when it designed and launched an artificial intelligence chatbot capable ...
articles.body_text:
The US states of Virginia and Oregon have sued Elon Musk’s SpaceX, saying the business harmed consumers by avoiding safeguards when it designed and launched an artificial intelligence chatbot capable of creating sexualised images.

The attorneys general of both states filed complaints in separate lawsuits on Monday.

Several states had announced investigations into Grok over similar claims in recent months, but Virginia and Oregon are the first states to sue.

The lawsuits filed in state courts accuse SpaceX of misleading consumers about Grok’s safety and failing to put adequate safeguards in place while promoting its “spicy mode”. The feature allows users to take an existing photograph of a person and generate a sexual or nude image or video, according to the lawsuits.

The company prioritised its business model over the safety of millions of people, Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said in his state’s lawsuit.

“To push its lagging product, Grok, to tens of millions of new users, it stripped out industry-standard safeguards and marketed a ‘spicy mode’ built to produce nudity,” Jones said in the lawsuit. “For these Defendants, weak safeguards were not a failure but a feature.”

Virginia and Oregon accused SpaceX of violating their respective consumer protection laws. They are seeking damages, penalties and court orders forcing the company to stop violating state law.

SpaceX did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Grok is available to users of X, the social media platform that is a subsidiary of SpaceX.

In a statement posted on X on Monday that did not directly address the lawsuits, the platform’s safety team said it had taken action to block prompts that could generate sexualised or nude imagery and worked with law enforcement to pursue people who use the platform to make it.

“The people who tried to use Grok Imagine to generate this material did so by deliberately violating our Terms of Service and working aggressively to circumvent our safeguards,” the company posted.

Virginia’s lawsuit cites data from a study by the Center for Countering Digital Hate, which estimated that between December 2025 and January 2026, Grok generated and posted millions of sexualised images on X, including more than 20,000 depicting children.

Investigators from the attorney general’s office in Virginia found that Grok’s image moderation was inconsistent, and that the bot would advise users on how to circumvent the moderation measures by avoiding words that triggered it, according to the lawsuit.

Beginning in January, Grok told users that its image generation features were only for paying subscribers, which did not stop the images’ creation but allowed the company to profit from them, the lawsuit said.

SpaceX is facing more than a dozen lawsuits brought by individuals who say nonconsensual sexual images of them as minors or adults were generated by Grok.

articles.title: Bessent gave Iran weeks before it had ‘nothing left to trade.’ New sanctions expose what survived
articles.excerpt: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent joins 'Sunday Morning Futures' to discuss the Trump administration's economic sanctions against Iran, predicting a swift collapse of the regime's economy. Bessent...
articles.body_text:
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent joins 'Sunday Morning Futures' to discuss the Trump administration's economic sanctions against Iran, predicting a swift collapse of the regime's economy. Bessent also addresses the Iranian death threats that forced his family to relocate to a military base and weighs in on the compliance failures at Nvidia amid its ongoing espionage probe.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned in September that Iran would have "nothing left to trade" within two weeks.

Nearly two months later, the Trump administration is still targeting the overseas financial networks Tehran has used to keep money moving despite sweeping U.S. sanctions in the midst of ongoing war.

On Monday, Treasury announced another round of sanctions targeting more than two dozen individuals and companies accused of helping Iran move billions of dollars through financial networks spanning Dubai, Hong Kong and Turkey.

Bessent has repeatedly warned that Iran is nearing economic collapse, describing successive crackdowns as steps toward cutting off the regime's remaining financial lifelines. Yet each new round of sanctions has exposed more of the networks Tehran has used to keep doing business abroad — even as mounting economic pressure has failed to produce a diplomatic breakthrough.

COULD IRAN’S REGIME COLLAPSE? EXPERTS ASSESS BESSENT’S BID TO SEVER FINANCIAL LIFELINES

Secretary Scott Bessent speaks to members of the media outside the White House in Washington, D.C., on Oct. 22, 2025 (Aaron Schwartz/CNP/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

While the administration says its blockade has largely stopped Iranian oil exports, Monday's sanctions detail how Tehran has relied on currency dealers, trading companies and middlemen to conduct business abroad.

Treasury identified approximately $14.7 billion in financial activity potentially linked to Iranian shadow banking between January 2025 and August 2026, underscoring the scale of the networks Washington is now targeting.

Just three days earlier, Treasury declared that Iran had exhausted its seaborne oil supply outside the U.S. blockade, saying no new oil had been loaded onto vessels since the launch of Operation Economic Outcast in August.

"The regime has exhausted its seaborne oil supply, and it may never see the revenue from the oil it has already sold. The ship is sinking," Bessent said Friday.

In a response to Fox News Digital, Treasury said Iran has not loaded a single barrel of oil onto vessels since Aug. 25, 2026, and claimed Tehran is struggling to access foreign currency and recover proceeds from previous oil sales.

The department also provided a report showing the Iranian rial has lost roughly 25% of its value since August, while inflation reached 90% in September. Treasury said it is continuing to target alternative financial channels, including cryptocurrency exchanges, as Tehran looks for ways around U.S. restrictions.

BESSENT SAYS IRAN WILL HAVE 'NOTHING LEFT TO TRADE' WITHIN TWO WEEKS AS OIL LIFELINE DRIES UP

A cargo ship sails in the Persian Gulf toward the Strait of Hormuz, April 22, 2026. (AP Photo)

But even as the administration claims success in cutting off new oil shipments, Treasury is still pursuing Iranian operatives accused of collecting billions of dollars from previous sales. Friday's sanctions targeted four individuals involved in recovering oil revenues held overseas, some of which Treasury said had been diverted by middlemen for personal gain.

Bessent's September prediction was hardly his first warning that Tehran was approaching an economic breaking point.

Months earlier, he said U.S. sanctions were "asphyxiating" Iran's economy and warned that the country could soon be forced to shut down oil wells as storage facilities filled up.

By late August, Bessent was predicting Iran's economy could collapse within "weeks or months," as the administration launched Operation Economic Outcast, a campaign aimed at cutting off the regime's remaining revenue.

The warnings continued in October, when Bessent projected Iran's economy could shrink by more than 25% over the year ending in March 2027. Earlier this month, he described the country as experiencing one of the fastest economic collapses in history.

BESSENT WARNS IRAN'S OUTSIDE BACKERS TO 'STAY AWAY' AS TRUMP SEEKS TO 'ASPHYXIATE' TEHRAN'S ECONOMY

The administration had increasingly turned to economic pressure after months of military strikes failed to force Tehran into an agreement. Washington reimposed its naval blockade in July after an interim deal collapsed, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in September that the price Iran would pay going forward would be primarily economic, although military action remained an option.

But neither the military campaign nor the mounting economic pressure has produced a broader agreement. Iran continues to demand sanctions relief, access to frozen assets and an end to the blockade, while Washington is pressing Tehran for concessions on its nuclear program and regional activities.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent speaks with reporters outside the White House, Wednesday, in Washington, D.C. (AP Photo/Evan Vucci)

Despite months of escalating pressure, Treasury is still identifying overseas financial networks that have allowed Iran to conduct business outside traditional banking channels.

Iran has spent decades developing ways around American financial restrictions, relying on middlemen, shell companies and foreign currency exchanges to keep trade flowing even as Washington moves to cut off its access to international markets.

Monday's announcement detailed some of those channels, including exchange houses and trading companies operating across Iran, the United Arab Emirates, Turkey and Hong Kong.

Among the newly sanctioned entities was an Iranian currency exchange center that Treasury says facilitates tens of billions of dollars in annual trade, connecting exporters holding foreign currency with importers seeking to purchase goods abroad.

articles.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine behind drone attacks on Russian ships near Libya
articles.excerpt: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukrainian forces sank ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠a Russian warship in Benghazi and also hit a cargo ship used to transport weapons off the coast of Libya, hailing an “exemplary Ukraini...
articles.body_text:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukrainian forces sank ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠a Russian warship in Benghazi and also hit a cargo ship used to transport weapons off the coast of Libya, hailing an “exemplary Ukrainian operation in response to Russia’s war”.

Ukraine’s president said  in a statement on Monday that the Merkury, one of Russia’s newest warships, sank after Ukrainian forces launched seven naval drones on Sunday. A KA-27 combat helicopter was also destroyed in the attack.

He confirmed that Ukraine’s forces also attacked the cargo ship Angara. Libya’s eastern health ministry in Benghazi said all crew members from the cargo ship had been rescued and were receiving treatment after Sunday’s attack.

Authorities in eastern Libya said the warship was docked in the port of Benghazi when the explosion occurred.

“We firmly reject the use of our territory or territorial waters as an arena for settling scores or as an extension of external conflicts,” Saddam Haftar, the deputy commander-in-chief of the eastern Libyan administration’s forces said.

“The security and sovereignty of Libya are a national responsibility that leaves no room for political posturing or the exploitation of incidents to propagate accusations and incite fear,” he said.

Reporting from Moscow, Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova said that Russian authorities have not yet made an official comment on the drone attack on the warship.

“According to the Libyan side, the ship was returning to Russia from its mission and stopped in Benghazi for refuelling,” our correspondent said. She said it was not clear if there were any casualties.

“Russian military infrastructure is Ukraine’s target, not just in Russia, but pretty much throughout the world,” she said.

The United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) expressed “serious concern” over the drone attacks, calling for “an immediate, independent and transparent investigation”.

“Libya cannot afford and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts,” UNSMIL wrote on X.

The eastern administration did not identify who was behind Sunday’s attack but said Libya was “not a party to the Russian-Ukrainian war”.

The oil-rich nation of Libya has been divided between the government in Tripoli and a rival administration in the east since the overthrow of longtime ruler Muammar Gaddafi in 2011.

articles.title: Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble hours after Russian strike on Ukraine, rescuers say
articles.excerpt:
'Danger seems greater all the time': Ukrainians search for missing after Russian strikes hit Kyiv

A seven-year-old boy has been rescued from the rubble of a residential building in Dymer, in the Kyiv...
articles.body_text:
'Danger seems greater all the time': Ukrainians search for missing after Russian strikes hit Kyiv

A seven-year-old boy has been rescued from the rubble of a residential building in Dymer, in the Kyiv region, after 14 hours. Overnight Russian strikes on the village killed 11 people, Ukrainian officials have said.

The attack occurred in the early hours of Sunday. A 79-year-old woman was also rescued alive from the collapsed building, Kyiv's regional head Tymur Tkachenko said.

A strike on a private home in Bila Tserkva killed one more person and set the building ablaze, he added.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also said three people were killed and 13 wounded in a separate strike on Vyshneve, also in the Kyiv region, that hit a grocery store on Sunday.

Ukrainian authorities said the boy in Dymer is in stable condition and was taken to hospital, and have thanked everyone involved in saving his life.

Zelensky and Ukraine's national police also confirmed the rescue of the boy.

In a Telegram post, Tkachenko said the 79-year-old woman rescued from the rubble was receiving treatment in hospital.

Earlier he said six people were injured in the attack, while others were still missing.

The attack on the residential building occurred in the early hours of the morning while people were asleep

Zelensky said more than 130 people are involved in emergency operations at the scene, and that they will continue until they have "complete information about every single person".

Sending his condolences to the families and loved ones of those killed, he said the strike struck the residential building, "practically blowing a section of it to smithereens".

Zelensky added that "rescue efforts are complicated by constant new air raid alerts and renewed threats".

The strike hit the building at 05:00 local time, when families were still asleep, Ukraine's minister of internal affairs Ivan Vyhivskyi said.

More than 70 strikes have been launched across 10 Ukrainian regions as of Sunday evening, Vyhivskyi added.

Emergency workers continue to search for those missing after Russian drone and missile attacks in Dymer.

In his video address posted online, Zelensky also said three people were killed and 13 injured in a strike on an "ordinary grocery store" in Vyshneve.

Mayor Illya Dikov wrote on social media that three children were among the injured.

Russia also struck a power substation in the Dnipropetrovsk region, Ukraine's Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky said in a post on X., external
